title: PRD: convert postmortem action items into operational SLA & escalation map for runtime incidents
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: After the Feb regional KV-cache incident, several postmortem actions require formalizing into the serving PRD so that product, ops, and engineering have a single source of truth for escalation, verification, and release gates. This ticket scopes the PRD updates: an operational SLA/escalation matrix, deployment-specific rollback criteria, synthetic verification hooks, and acceptance tests that will be required before enabling new serving features (kernel updates, batching changes, quantization profiles).

Goals:
- Translate postmortem action items into discrete PRD requirements that are actionable for runtime, infra, and console teams.
- Ensure acceptance criteria are testable and automatable where possible (synthetic checks, CI job definitions, canary verification).
- Define an escalation map that ties incident severity to ownership, SLO degradation thresholds, and communication/playbook steps across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment modes.
- Specify rollback and partial-deploy gates linked to metrics (tail-latency p95/p99, KV-cache regen rate, error budget burn rate).

Scope (in-scope):
- PRD language additions and requirement clauses for: 
  * Escalation matrix (severity -> owner -> SLA gates -> runbook step links)
  * Acceptance tests and synthetic verification definitions (what passes/fails, sampling windows, thresholds)
  * Deployment-specific gating for runtime changes (canary traffic %, rollback criteria, automatic fallback model mappings)
  * Observability requirements (dashboards, tracing hooks, alert thresholds with concrete values)
  * Documentation links and required artifacts (runbooks, playbooks, post-deploy checks)

Out-of-scope: full implementation work for engines, infra changes, or operator runbook automation. This ticket produces the PRD and acceptance-test definitions to hand off to engineering stories.
acceptance_criteria: A clear escalation matrix table included in PRD listing incident severity levels (SEV1-SEV4), primary owners, on-call rotations, minimum SLAs, and communication templates.

For each deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), PRD defines explicit rollback gates tied to numeric thresholds: p99 latency increase %, KV-cache regen frequency, error-rate delta, or capacity exhaustion signals.

Synthetic verification harness defined with at least three scenarios (cold-start KV-cache regen, high-concurrency batching, kernel regression) and pass/fail thresholds; links to CI jobs and expected runtime durations.
Acceptance tests phrased as automated checks (CI + synthetic) and manual runbook steps; each test includes required preconditions, execution steps, expected outcomes, and remediation actions.
Observable metrics and dashboard templates are specified (metric name, aggregation window, alert threshold, threshold rationale) so SRE can implement alerts without additional ambiguity.
Runbook links and handoffs: each escalation step references a canonical runbook (Confluence path) and a GitHub playbook PR for operator scripts; PRD must list owners for maintenance cadence.
Security and compliance considerations for Private deployments documented (KMS interactions, audit-log retention impact on error budgets) and flagged if additional review is required.
comments: 2026-03-03 Maya Chen: Drafted scope from postmortem (INC-2026-02-kvcache). Focused on making requirements testable; want SRE and runtime leads to verify numeric thresholds are realistic.

2026-03-05 Ethan Rodriguez: Added initial rollback gates proposal: trigger when p99 latency increases by >30% sustained for 3 minutes OR KV-cache regen rate exceeds 10/minute for 2 minutes. Marking as candidate values — request engineering feedback.
2026-03-07 Priya Singh (SRE): Confirmed synthetic scenario templates are feasible. Suggested adding a warm-pool size check for Dedicated to avoid coldstart cascades. Will add dashboard mockups.

2026-03-09 Alex Morales (Runtime): Proposed replacing fixed p99 delta with a normalized baseline approach (rolling baseline over last 1h) to reduce false positives during legitimate traffic shifts. Added note to acceptance criteria to allow baseline-based thresholds.

2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Incorporated Alex's baseline suggestion and added requirement that PRD include guidance for when to escalate to cross-region failover (latency + error budget conditions). Ready for PM + SRE sign-off.

2026-03-11 Product review: Requested explicit listing of artifacts to hand off to engineering (CI job names, synthetic harness repo, dashboard IDs). Also requested timeline for implementing acceptance tests as part of release readiness gating.
